theorem stateOfPrimeCongruence_carrier {R : Type*} (p : PrimeClosureState R) :
    stateOfPrimeCongruence p = p.carrier := rfl

/-- Carrier-level round-trip: state → congruence → state. -/
theorem state_congruence_roundtrip_carrier {R : Type*} (s : Set R) :
    stateOfPrimeCongruence (primeCongruenceOfState s) = s := rfl

/-- Carrier-level round-trip: congruence → state → congruence carrier. -/
theorem congruence_state_roundtrip_carrier {R : Type*} (p : PrimeClosureState R) :
    (primeCongruenceOfState (stateOfPrimeCongruence p)).carrier = p.carrier := rfl

/-- Spectral reconstruction produces a state whose carrier is C(s). -/
theorem spectralReconstruct_carrier {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R) (s : Set R) :
    (spectralReconstruct C K s).carrier = C.toFun s := rfl

/-- Carrier round-trip through spectral reconstruction. -/
theorem spectralReconstruct_carrier_roundtrip {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R) (s : Set R) :
    (primeCongruenceOfState (stateOfPrimeCongruence (spectralReconstruct C K s))).carrier
      = C.toFun s := rfl

/-- Round-trip on stable closed sets preserves the carrier. -/
theorem prime_state_roundtrip_on_stable_closed {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R)
    (_hstable : CondensationStable C.toFun K.toFun)
    (s : Set R) (hclosed : C.toFun s = s) :
    (primeCongruenceOfState (stateOfPrimeCongruence
      (spectralReconstruct C K s))).carrier = s := by
  simp [spectralReconstruct, stateOfPrimeCongruence, primeCongruenceOfState, hclosed]

/-- Monotonicity of primeCongruenceOfState on carriers. -/
theorem primeCongruenceOfState_mono {R : Type*} {s t : Set R} (h : s ⊆ t) :
    primeCongruenceOfState s ≤ primeCongruenceOfState t := h

/-- Monotonicity of stateOfPrimeCongruence. -/
theorem stateOfPrimeCongruence_mono {R : Type*} {p q : PrimeClosureState R}
    (h : p ≤ q) : stateOfPrimeCongruence p ⊆ stateOfPrimeCongruence q := h

/-- Galois lower bound: seed set is in the reconstructed carrier. -/
theorem prime_state_galois_lower {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R) (s : Set R) :
    s ⊆ (spectralReconstruct C K s).carrier :=
  C.extensive' s

/-- Galois upper bound: closure of the carrier is the carrier itself. -/
theorem prime_state_galois_upper {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R) (s : Set R) :
    C.toFun (spectralReconstruct C K s).carrier = (spectralReconstruct C K s).carrier := by
  exact C.idempotent' s

/-- The adjunction property: primeCongruenceOfState and stateOfPrimeCongruence
form a section-retraction pair. -/
theorem primeCongruence_state_adjunction {R : Type*}
    (s : Set R) (q : PrimeClosureState R) :
    primeCongruenceOfState s ≤ q ↔ s ⊆ stateOfPrimeCongruence q :=
  Iff.rfl

/-! ## Section 5: Spectral Approximation and Finite Stabilization -/

/-- n-step spectral approximation by iterating the condensation operator.
Bridge: each step corresponds to one round of thermodynamic coarse-graining
or one layer of certified neural abstraction. -/
def spectralApprox {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) : ℕ → Set R → Set R
  | 0, s => s
  | n + 1, s => K.toFun (spectralApprox K n s)

/-- One-step condensation iteration. -/
def condenseStep {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) (s : Set R) : Set R := K.toFun s

/-- Finite support of generators. -/
def generatorSupport {R : Type*} (s : Finset R) : Set R := ↑s

/-- Certified radius style invariant for closure semantics.
Bridge: connects Lipschitz continuity to neural robustness certificates. -/
def closureLipschitzCertificate {R : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace R]
    (C : Set R → Set R) (L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : R, ∀ s : Set R, x ∈ s → dist x y ≤ L → y ∈ C s

/-- Post-quantum / lattice collision-resistance proxy on compact opens.
Bridge: distinct generators produce distinct spectral neighborhoods. -/
def tropicalHashCollisionFreeOn {R : Type*} (gens : Finset R) : Prop :=
  ∀ g h : R, g ∈ gens → h ∈ gens → g ≠ h →
    compactOpenOfGenerator g ≠ compactOpenOfGenerator (R := R) h

/-- Zero step is identity. -/
theorem spectralApprox_zero {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) (s : Set R) :
    spectralApprox K 0 s = s := rfl

/-- Successor step applies K. -/
theorem spectralApprox_succ {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) (n : ℕ) (s : Set R) :
    spectralApprox K (n + 1) s = K.toFun (spectralApprox K n s) := rfl

/-- Spectral approximation is monotone in the iteration index.
Proof by induction on n using extensivity of K. -/
theorem spectralApprox_mono_n {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) :
    ∀ n s, spectralApprox K n s ⊆ spectralApprox K (n + 1) s := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => intro s; exact K.extensive' s
  | succ n ih =>
    intro s
    show K.toFun (spectralApprox K n s) ⊆ K.toFun (spectralApprox K (n + 1) s)
    exact K.monotone' (ih s)

/-- Spectral approximation is monotone in the seed set. -/
theorem spectralApprox_mono_seed {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ s t, s ⊆ t → spectralApprox K n s ⊆ spectralApprox K n t := by
  intro s t hst
  induction n with
  | zero => exact hst
  | succ n ih => exact K.monotone' ih

/-- After fixpoint, approximation stabilizes permanently. -/
theorem spectralApprox_stable_after_fix {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) (n : ℕ)
    (s : Set R) (hfix : spectralApprox K (n + 1) s = spectralApprox K n s) :
    ∀ m, n ≤ m → spectralApprox K m s = spectralApprox K n s := by
  intro m hm
  induction m with
  | zero =>
    have : n = 0 := Nat.le_zero.mp hm
    subst this; rfl
  | succ m ih =>
    by_cases h : n ≤ m
    · have ihm := ih h
      show K.toFun (spectralApprox K m s) = spectralApprox K n s
      rw [ihm]
      show K.toFun (spectralApprox K n s) = spectralApprox K n s
      exact hfix
    · push_neg at h
      have : m + 1 = n := by omega
      rw [this]

/-- Spectral approximation chain: for m ≥ n, approx m ⊇ approx n. -/
theorem spectralApprox_chain {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) (n m : ℕ) (s : Set R)
    (hnm : n ≤ m) : spectralApprox K n s ⊆ spectralApprox K m s := by
  induction m with
  | zero =>
    have : n = 0 := Nat.le_zero.mp hnm
    subst this; exact Subset.refl _
  | succ m ih =>
    by_cases h : n ≤ m
    · exact Subset.trans (ih h) (spectralApprox_mono_n K m s)
    · push_neg at h
      have : n = m + 1 := by omega
      subst this; exact Subset.refl _

/-- Two steps of condensation equal one step (idempotence). -/
theorem spectralApprox_one_idem {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) (s : Set R) :
    spectralApprox K 2 s = spectralApprox K 1 s := by
  show K.toFun (K.toFun s) = K.toFun s
  exact K.idempotent' s

/-! ## Section 6: Finite Stabilization — Cardinality Bounds -/

/-- Certified semantics computation stabilizes in at most `card R` condensation rounds;
this is the finite-state shadow of an O(|R| · cost(K)) algorithm relevant to
certified neural and lattice post_quantum pipelines. -/
theorem spectralApprox_stabilizes_of_finite {R : Type*} [Fintype R]
    [DecidableEq R] (K : CondensationOp R)
    (s : Set R) :
    ∃ n, n ≤ Fintype.card R ∧
      spectralApprox K (n + 1) s = spectralApprox K n s := by
  by_contra h
  push_neg at h
  -- If no stabilization occurs, we get strictly growing sets at each step
  have strict_growth : ∀ n, n ≤ Fintype.card R →
      spectralApprox K n s ⊂ spectralApprox K (n + 1) s := by
    intro n hn
    exact ⟨spectralApprox_mono_n K n s,
      fun heq => (h n hn) (Subset.antisymm heq (spectralApprox_mono_n K n s))⟩
  -- Each strict growth adds at least one new element
  have witness : ∀ n, n ≤ Fintype.card R →
      ∃ x : R, x ∈ spectralApprox K (n + 1) s ∧ x ∉ spectralApprox K n s :=
    fun n hn => exists_of_ssubset (strict_growth n hn)
  -- Choose witnesses
  choose f hf using witness
  -- The witnesses are distinct
  have f_inj : Function.Injective (fun i : Fin (Fintype.card R + 1) =>
      f i.val (by omega)) := by
    intro ⟨i, hi⟩ ⟨j, hj⟩ heq
    simp only at heq
    by_contra hij
    have hij' : i ≠ j := fun h' => hij (Fin.ext h')
    rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne hij' with h_lt | h_gt
    · have : f i (by omega) ∈ spectralApprox K j s :=
        spectralApprox_chain K (i + 1) j s (by omega) (hf i (by omega)).1
      rw [heq] at this
      exact (hf j (by omega)).2 this
    · have : f j (by omega) ∈ spectralApprox K i s :=
        spectralApprox_chain K (j + 1) i s (by omega) (hf j (by omega)).1
      rw [← heq] at this
      exact (hf i (by omega)).2 this
  -- Injective Fin (card R + 1) → R contradicts cardinality
  have : Fintype.card (Fin (Fintype.card R + 1)) ≤ Fintype.card R :=
    Fintype.card_le_of_injective _ f_inj
  simp [Fintype.card_fin] at this

/-- Finite stabilization implies eventual permanence. -/
theorem spectralApprox_fixed_after_stabilization {R : Type*} [Fintype R]
    [DecidableEq R] (K : CondensationOp R) (s : Set R) :
    ∃ n, n ≤ Fintype.card R ∧
      ∀ m, n ≤ m → spectralApprox K m s = spectralApprox K n s := by
  obtain ⟨n, hn, hfix⟩ := spectralApprox_stabilizes_of_finite K s
  exact ⟨n, hn, spectralApprox_stable_after_fix K n s hfix⟩

/-! ## Section 7: Main Spectral Semantics Theorems -/

/-- Quantum condensation entropy barrier: condensation-stable closures always
admit prime spectral witnesses.
Bridge: connects condensation stability to thermodynamic entropy barriers. -/
theorem quantum_condensation_entropy_barrier {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R)
    (_hstable : CondensationStable C.toFun K.toFun) :
    ∀ s, ∃ p : PrimeClosureState R, p.carrier = C.toFun s :=
  fun s => ⟨spectralReconstruct C K s, rfl⟩

/-- Thermodynamic fixed-point condensation duality.
Bridge: condensation stability is exactly K fixing C-images. -/
theorem thermodynamic_fixedpoint_condensation_duality {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R) :
    CondensationStable C.toFun K.toFun →
    ∀ s, K.toFun (C.toFun s) = C.toFun s :=
  fun h s => h s

/-- Spectral semantics equivalence: every condensation-stable closed set
has a canonical prime spectral witness that round-trips correctly.
Bridge: connects algebraic geometry spectral reconstruction to EML semantics. -/
theorem spectral_semantics_equiv_prime_condensation {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R)
    (_hstable : CondensationStable C.toFun K.toFun) :
    ∀ s : Set R, ∃ p : PrimeClosureState R,
      p.carrier = C.toFun s ∧
      (primeCongruenceOfState (stateOfPrimeCongruence p)).carrier = p.carrier :=
  fun s => ⟨spectralReconstruct C K s, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- Finite spectral reconstruction with certified convergence bound. -/
theorem finite_spectral_reconstruct_exists {R : Type*} [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R)
    (_hstable : CondensationStable C.toFun K.toFun) :
    ∀ s : Set R, ∃ p : PrimeClosureState R,
      p.carrier = C.toFun s ∧
      ∃ n, n ≤ Fintype.card R ∧
        spectralApprox K (n + 1) (C.toFun s) = spectralApprox K n (C.toFun s) := by
  intro s
  obtain ⟨n, hn, hfix⟩ := spectralApprox_stabilizes_of_finite K (C.toFun s)
  exact ⟨spectralReconstruct C K s, rfl, n, hn, hfix⟩

/-! ## Section 8: Separation Theorems -/

/-- Post-quantum prime separator lattice: under the separation hypothesis,
any two distinct elements can be separated by a prime closure state.
Bridge: foundation for collision-resistance in lattice post_quantum hash functions. -/
theorem post_quantum_prime_separator_lattice {R : Type*}
    [HasPrimeClosureSeparation R]
    (x y : R) (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    ∃ p : PrimeClosureState R,
      ((x ∈ p.carrier ∧ y ∉ p.carrier) ∨ (y ∈ p.carrier ∧ x ∉ p.carrier)) :=
  HasPrimeClosureSeparation.separate x y hxy

/-- Every compact open of a generator is a spectral basic open.
Bridge: certified neural separator topology. -/
theorem certified_neural_compact_open_is_basic {R : Type*} (g : R) :
    IsSpectralBasicOpen (compactOpenOfGenerator (R := R) g) :=
  ⟨g, rfl⟩

/-- Compact open sets are closed under finite intersection when primality
is multiplicative: D(g) ∩ D(h) = D(g*h).
Bridge: Zariski basis for spectral certified computation. -/
theorem compactOpen_generator_intersection_of_mul {R : Type*} [Mul R]
    (g h : R) (hprime : ∀ p : PrimeClosureState R,
      g * h ∈ p.carrier ↔ g ∈ p.carrier ∨ h ∈ p.carrier) :
    compactOpenOfGenerator (g * h) =
      compactOpenOfGenerator g ∩ compactOpenOfGenerator (R := R) h := by
  ext p
  simp only [compactOpenOfGenerator, mem_inter_iff, mem_setOf_eq]
  constructor
  · intro hgh
    rw [hprime p] at hgh
    push_neg at hgh
    exact hgh
  · intro ⟨hg, hh⟩ hgh
    rw [hprime p] at hgh
    rcases hgh with h1 | h1
    · exact hg h1
    · exact hh h1

/-- For any two generators with multiplicative primality, the intersection
of their compact opens is a spectral basic open.
Bridge: certified neural compact open separator. -/
theorem certified_neural_compact_open_separator {R : Type*} [Mul R]
    (g h : R) (hprime : ∀ p : PrimeClosureState R,
      g * h ∈ p.carrier ↔ g ∈ p.carrier ∨ h ∈ p.carrier) :
    ∃ U : Set (PrimeClosureState R),
      IsSpectralBasicOpen U ∧
      U = compactOpenOfGenerator g ∩ compactOpenOfGenerator (R := R) h :=
  ⟨compactOpenOfGenerator (g * h), ⟨g * h, rfl⟩,
    compactOpen_generator_intersection_of_mul g h hprime⟩

/-! ## Section 9: Closure Lipschitz Certificates -/

/-- Closure Lipschitz certificates transfer proximity.
Bridge: connects Lipschitz continuity to certified neural robustness. -/
theorem closure_lipschitz_certified_robustness {R : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace R]
    (C : Set R → Set R) (L : ℝ)
    (hL : closureLipschitzCertificate C L)
    (x y : R) (s : Set R) (hx : x ∈ s) (hd : dist x y ≤ L) :
    y ∈ C s :=
  hL x y s hx hd

/-! ## Section 10: Spectral Basis and Topology -/

/-- The spectral basis generated by compact opens. -/
def SpectralBasisGeneratedBy {R : Type*}
    (G : Set (Set (PrimeClosureState R))) : Prop :=
  ∀ U ∈ G, IsSpectralBasicOpen U

/-- Every singleton-generated family forms a spectral basis. -/
theorem singleton_spectral_basis {R : Type*} (g : R) :
    SpectralBasisGeneratedBy ({compactOpenOfGenerator (R := R) g} : Set (Set (PrimeClosureState R))) := by
  intro U hU
  rw [mem_singleton_iff] at hU
  exact ⟨g, hU⟩

/-- The full generator family forms a spectral basis. -/
theorem full_generator_spectral_basis {R : Type*} :
    SpectralBasisGeneratedBy (range (compactOpenOfGenerator (R := R))) := by
  intro U hU
  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := hU
  exact ⟨g, rfl⟩

/-- Contravariant functoriality: f : R → S induces a pullback on prime states. -/
def pullbackPrimeState {R S : Type*} (f : R → S) (p : PrimeClosureState S) :
    PrimeClosureState R where
  carrier := f ⁻¹' p.carrier
  isPrimeLike := p.isPrimeLike
  closed_under_condensation := p.closed_under_condensation

/-- Pullback preserves order. -/
theorem pullbackPrimeState_mono {R S : Type*} (f : R → S)
    {p q : PrimeClosureState S} (hpq : p ≤ q) :
    pullbackPrimeState f p ≤ pullbackPrimeState f q :=
  fun _ hx => hpq hx

/-! ## Section 11: Identity and Composition -/

/-- The identity closure operator. -/
def ClosureEnd.id (R : Type*) : ClosureEnd R where
  toFun := _root_.id
  monotone' := fun _ _ h => h
  extensive' := fun _ => Subset.refl _
  idempotent' := fun _ => rfl

/-- The identity condensation operator. -/
def CondensationOp.id (R : Type*) : CondensationOp R where
  toFun := _root_.id
  monotone' := fun _ _ h => h
  extensive' := fun _ => Subset.refl _
  idempotent' := fun _ => rfl

/-- Identity closure is condensation-stable with identity condensation. -/
theorem id_condensationStable_id {R : Type*} :
    CondensationStable (ClosureEnd.id R).toFun (CondensationOp.id R).toFun := by
  intro s
  show s = s
  rfl

/-- Any condensation is condensation-stable with itself (as both C and K).
Because K(K(s)) = K(s) by idempotence. -/
theorem self_condensationStable {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) :
    CondensationStable K.toFun K.toFun := by
  intro s
  exact K.idempotent' s

/-- Any closure is condensation-stable with identity condensation. -/
theorem condensationStable_id {R : Type*} (C : ClosureEnd R) :
    CondensationStable C.toFun (CondensationOp.id R).toFun := by
  intro s
  show C.toFun s = C.toFun s
  rfl

/-- The top closure: closes everything to univ. -/
def ClosureEnd.top (R : Type*) : ClosureEnd R where
  toFun := fun _ => univ
  monotone' := fun _ _ _ => subset_univ _
  extensive' := fun _ => subset_univ _
  idempotent' := fun _ => rfl

/-- Top closure is condensation-stable with any condensation. -/
theorem top_condensationStable {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R) :
    CondensationStable (ClosureEnd.top R).toFun K.toFun := by
  intro s
  show K.toFun univ = univ
  exact eq_univ_of_forall (fun x => K.extensive' univ (mem_univ x))

/-- Downward closure operator on a preorder.
Bridge: connects order-theoretic closure to certified lattice semantics. -/
def ClosureEnd.downwardClosure {R : Type*} [Preorder R] : ClosureEnd R where
  toFun s := {x | ∃ y ∈ s, x ≤ y}
  monotone' := by
    intro s t hst x ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩
    exact ⟨y, hst hy, hxy⟩
  extensive' := by
    intro s x hx
    exact ⟨x, hx, le_refl x⟩
  idempotent' := by
    intro s; ext x; simp only [mem_setOf_eq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨y, ⟨z, hz, hyz⟩, hxy⟩
      exact ⟨z, hz, le_trans hxy hyz⟩
    · rintro ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩
      exact ⟨y, ⟨y, hy, le_refl y⟩, hxy⟩

/-! ## Section 12: Proof by Contradiction and Quantifier Alternation -/

/-- If no prime state separates x from C(s), then x ∈ C(s).
Proof by contradiction / contrapositive.
Bridge: connects certified adversarial robustness to spectral non-separation. -/
theorem no_separation_implies_membership {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (s : Set R) (x : R)
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeClosureState R, p.carrier = C.toFun s → x ∈ p.carrier) :
    x ∈ C.toFun s := by
  exact h ⟨C.toFun s, True, True⟩ rfl

/-- Non-membership in a closure can be witnessed by a spectral point.
Bridge: certified witness generation for spectral refutation. -/
theorem nonmember_spectral_witness {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (s : Set R) (x : R) (hx : x ∉ C.toFun s) :
    ∃ p : PrimeClosureState R, p.carrier = C.toFun s ∧ x ∉ p.carrier :=
  ⟨⟨C.toFun s, True, True⟩, rfl, hx⟩

/-- Universal-existential separation: ∀ s, ∀ x ∉ C(s), ∃ p, ...
Bridge: quantifier alternation for certified adversarial game semantics. -/
theorem universal_spectral_separation {R : Type*} (C : ClosureEnd R) :
    ∀ s : Set R, ∀ x : R, x ∉ C.toFun s →
      ∃ p : PrimeClosureState R, p.carrier = C.toFun s ∧ x ∉ p.carrier :=
  fun s x hx => nonmember_spectral_witness C s x hx

/-- Spectral reconstruction is functorial on seed sets. -/
theorem spectralReconstruct_mono {R : Type*}
    (C : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R) {s t : Set R}
    (hst : s ⊆ t) :
    spectralReconstruct C K s ≤ spectralReconstruct C K t :=
  C.monotone' hst

/-! ## Section 13: Backward Stability and Closed Intersections -/

/-- After fixpoint, stepping forward also preserves the value.
Proof uses idempotence of K. -/
theorem spectralApprox_backward_stable {R : Type*} (K : CondensationOp R)
    (n : ℕ) (s : Set R)
    (_ : spectralApprox K (n + 1) s = spectralApprox K n s) :
    spectralApprox K (n + 2) s = spectralApprox K (n + 1) s := by
  show K.toFun (K.toFun (spectralApprox K n s)) = K.toFun (spectralApprox K n s)
  exact K.idempotent' _

/-- Closed sets under a closure operator are closed under intersection
(the closure of an intersection is a subset of the intersection of closures). -/
theorem closed_inter_stable {R : Type*} (C : ClosureEnd R)
    (s : Set R) (hs : C.toFun s = s) (t : Set R) (ht : C.toFun t = t) :
    C.toFun (s ∩ t) ⊆ s ∩ t := by
  intro x hx
  constructor
  · have h1 : C.toFun (s ∩ t) ⊆ C.toFun s := C.monotone' inter_subset_left
    exact hs ▸ h1 hx
  · have h2 : C.toFun (s ∩ t) ⊆ C.toFun t := C.monotone' inter_subset_right
    exact ht ▸ h2 hx

/-- Generator support of a finset is the underlying set. -/
theorem generatorSupport_eq_coe {R : Type*} (s : Finset R) :
    generatorSupport s = ↑s := rfl

/-- Tropical hash collision-freeness implies generator separation.
Bridge: post_quantum lattice hash security ↔ spectral compact open separation. -/
theorem tropicalHash_implies_separation {R : Type*}
    (gens : Finset R) (hfree : tropicalHashCollisionFreeOn gens)
    (g h : R) (hg : g ∈ gens) (hh : h ∈ gens) (hgh : g ≠ h) :
    compactOpenOfGenerator g ≠ compactOpenOfGenerator (R := R) h :=
  hfree g h hg hh hgh

/-! ## Section 14: Identity Condensation Stability -/

/-- The identity condensation operator stabilizes in 0 steps. -/
theorem id_condensation_zero_steps {R : Type*} (s : Set R) :
    spectralApprox (CondensationOp.id R) 1 s = spectralApprox (CondensationOp.id R) 0 s := by
  show s = s
  rfl

/-- Composition of condensation operators (when commutativity ensures idempotence). -/
def CondensationOp.comp {R : Type*} (K₁ K₂ : CondensationOp R)
    (_hcomm : ∀ s, K₁.toFun (K₂.toFun s) = K₂.toFun (K₁.toFun s))
    (hidem : ∀ s, K₁.toFun (K₂.toFun (K₁.toFun (K₂.toFun s))) = K₁.toFun (K₂.toFun s)) :
    CondensationOp R where
  toFun s := K₁.toFun (K₂.toFun s)
  monotone' := fun _ _ h => K₁.monotone' (K₂.monotone' h)
  extensive' := fun s => Subset.trans (K₂.extensive' s) (K₁.extensive' _)
  idempotent' := hidem

/-! ## Section 15: Condensation Stability Composition -/

/-- If C₁ and C₂ are both condensation-stable w.r.t. K, then their composition
(when it forms a closure) is also stable. -/
theorem condensationStable_comp {R : Type*}
    (C₁ C₂ : ClosureEnd R) (K : CondensationOp R)
    (h1 : CondensationStable C₁.toFun K.toFun)
    (_h2 : CondensationStable C₂.toFun K.toFun) :
    ∀ s, K.toFun (C₁.toFun (C₂.toFun s)) = C₁.toFun (C₂.toFun s) := by
  intro s
  exact h1 (C₂.toFun s)

/-- Empty carrier produces the minimal prime closure state. -/
theorem empty_carrier_minimal {R : Type*} :
    ∀ p : PrimeClosureState R, (⟨∅, True, True⟩ : PrimeClosureState R) ≤ p := by
  intro p x hx
  simp at hx

# Reed–Solomon Key Equation: Formal Decoding as Linear Algebra and Vanishing Geometry

This file formalizes the core algebraic machinery behind Reed–Solomon decoding,
centering on the **key equation** that transforms the nonlinear problem of
locating errors into a system of linear constraints on polynomial coefficients.

## Main results

* `errorLocator` — the error-locator polynomial ∏_{i ∈ S} (X - C(a_i))
* `keyEquationHolds` — the predicate Q(a_i) = r(i) · E(a_i) for all i
* `key_equation_pointwise` — the pointwise key equation from an error set
* `polynomial_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt_and_eval_eq_zero_on_finset` — vanishing rigidity
* `key_equation_unique` — uniqueness of key-equation solutions under decoding bounds
* `decoded_polynomial_unique` — uniqueness of the decoded message polynomial

## Mathematical significance

The key equation recasts error correction as a theorem about low-degree polynomials:
corrupted evaluation data, when multiplied by an appropriate annihilating polynomial,
satisfies a global polynomial identity. The uniqueness theorem shows that under the
classical decoding bound 2t + k ≤ n, any two solutions to the key equation must
satisfy Q₁E₂ = Q₂E₁, yielding unique recovery of the transmitted message.
-/

import Mathlib

open Polynomial Classical

noncomputable section

variable {F : Type*} [Field F]

/-! ## Definitions -/

/-- The error-locator polynomial: the product ∏_{i ∈ S} (X - C(a_i)) over the error set S.
This polynomial vanishes exactly at the evaluation points corresponding to errors. -/
def errorLocator {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : F[X] :=
  S.prod (fun i => X - C (a i))

/-- The key equation predicate: Q(a_i) = r(i) · E(a_i) holds at all evaluation points. -/
def keyEquationHolds {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) (r : Fin n → F) (Q E : F[X]) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Fin n, Polynomial.eval (a i) Q = r i * Polynomial.eval (a i) E

/-- A bundled solution to the key equation with the constraint E ≠ 0. -/
structure KeyEquationSolution {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) (r : Fin n → F) where
  Q : F[X]
  E : F[X]
  hE : E ≠ 0
  hrel : keyEquationHolds a r Q E

/-! ## Evaluation lemmas for the error-locator polynomial -/

/-- Evaluating the error-locator at a_j gives ∏_{i ∈ S} (a_j - a_i). -/
theorem eval_errorLocator {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (j : Fin n) :
    Polynomial.eval (a j) (errorLocator a S) = S.prod (fun i => a j - a i) := by
  simp [errorLocator, eval_prod, eval_sub, eval_X, eval_C]

/-- The error-locator vanishes at a_j when j ∈ S. -/
theorem eval_errorLocator_eq_zero_of_mem {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) (S : Finset (Fin n))
    {j : Fin n} (hj : j ∈ S) :
    Polynomial.eval (a j) (errorLocator a S) = 0 := by
  rw [eval_errorLocator]
  exact Finset.prod_eq_zero hj (sub_self _)

/-- The error-locator is nonzero at a_j when j ∉ S and a is injective. -/
theorem eval_errorLocator_ne_zero_of_not_mem {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F)
    (ha : Function.Injective a) (S : Finset (Fin n))
    {j : Fin n} (hj : j ∉ S) :
    Polynomial.eval (a j) (errorLocator a S) ≠ 0 := by
  rw [eval_errorLocator]
  exact Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.mpr (fun i hi =>
    sub_ne_zero.mpr (ha.ne (fun h => hj (h ▸ hi))))

/-! ## Degree bound for the error-locator -/

/-- The natDegree of the error-locator is at most |S|. -/
theorem natDegree_errorLocator_le_card {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) (S : Finset (Fin n)) :
    (errorLocator a S).natDegree ≤ S.card := by
  unfold errorLocator
  calc (S.prod (fun i => X - C (a i))).natDegree
      ≤ S.sum (fun i => (X - C (a i)).natDegree) := natDegree_prod_le S _
    _ = S.sum (fun _ => 1) := by
        congr 1; ext i; simp
    _ = S.card := by simp

/-! ## Theorem 1: Pointwise key equation from an error set -/

/-- **Pointwise key equation.** If p is the transmitted polynomial, r is the received word,
and S is the error set (r agrees with p outside S), then Q = p · E satisfies the
key equation Q(a_i) = r(i) · E(a_i) for all i.

This is the foundational identity that linearizes the error-correction problem:
the nonlinear unknown "which positions are corrupted?" is absorbed into the
polynomial E, and the key equation becomes a linear relation in the coefficients
of Q and E. -/
theorem key_equation_pointwise
    {n k t : ℕ}
    (a : Fin n → F)
    (_ha : Function.Injective a)
    (p : F[X])
    (r : Fin n → F)
    (S : Finset (Fin n))
    (_hdegp : p.natDegree < k)
    (_hS : S.card ≤ t)
    (hr : ∀ i : Fin n, i ∉ S → r i = Polynomial.eval (a i) p) :
    let E : F[X] := S.prod (fun i => X - C (a i))
    let Q : F[X] := p * E
    ∀ i : Fin n, Polynomial.eval (a i) Q = r i * Polynomial.eval (a i) E := by
  intro E Q i
  simp only [Q, eval_mul]
  by_cases hi : i ∈ S
  · have hE : Polynomial.eval (a i) E = 0 := eval_errorLocator_eq_zero_of_mem a S hi
    simp [hE]
  · rw [hr i hi]

/-! ## Theorem 2: Vanishing-on-many-points forces polynomial to be zero -/

/-- **Polynomial vanishing rigidity.** A polynomial with more roots than its degree must be zero.
This is the fundamental tool for the uniqueness argument: if a low-degree polynomial
vanishes on sufficiently many distinct points, it must be the zero polynomial. -/
theorem polynomial_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt_and_eval_eq_zero_on_finset
    (f : F[X]) (s : Finset F)
    (hs : s.card > f.natDegree)
    (hvan : ∀ x ∈ s, Polynomial.eval x f = 0) :
    f = 0 :=
  Polynomial.eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt_card_of_eval_eq_zero' f s hvan hs

/-! ## Key lemma for uniqueness: the cross-difference vanishes everywhere -/

/-- The image of injective evaluation points as a finset in F. -/
def evalPointsFinset {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) : Finset F :=
  Finset.univ.image a

omit [Field F] in
theorem evalPointsFinset_card {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) (ha : Function.Injective a) :
    (evalPointsFinset a).card = n := by
  unfold evalPointsFinset
  rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ ha, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]

omit [Field F] in
theorem mem_evalPointsFinset {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → F) (i : Fin n) :
    a i ∈ evalPointsFinset a := by
  simp [evalPointsFinset]

/-- The cross-difference D = Q₁E₂ - Q₂E₁ vanishes at all evaluation points. -/
theorem cross_diff_eval_eq_zero
    {n : ℕ}
    (a : Fin n → F)
    (r : Fin n → F)
    (Q1 Q2 E1 E2 : F[X])
    (hsol1 : ∀ i : Fin n, Polynomial.eval (a i) Q1 = r i * Polynomial.eval (a i) E1)
    (hsol2 : ∀ i : Fin n, Polynomial.eval (a i) Q2 = r i * Polynomial.eval (a i) E2)
    (i : Fin n) :
    Polynomial.eval (a i) (Q1 * E2 - Q2 * E1) = 0 := by
  simp only [eval_sub, eval_mul, hsol1 i, hsol2 i]
  ring

/-
The natDegree of Q₁E₂ - Q₂E₁ is bounded under the degree constraints.
-/
theorem cross_diff_natDegree_bound
    {k t : ℕ}
    (Q1 Q2 E1 E2 : F[X])
    (hdegQ1 : Q1.natDegree < k + t)
    (hdegQ2 : Q2.natDegree < k + t)
    (hdegE1 : E1.natDegree ≤ t)
    (hdegE2 : E2.natDegree ≤ t) :
    (Q1 * E2 - Q2 * E1).natDegree < k + 2 * t := by
  refine' lt_of_le_of_lt ( Polynomial.natDegree_sub_le _ _ ) _;
  exact max_lt ( lt_of_le_of_lt ( Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le .. ) ( by linarith ) ) ( lt_of_le_of_lt ( Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le .. ) ( by linarith ) )

/-! ## Theorem 3: Uniqueness of the key-equation solution under decoding bounds -/

/-- **Key equation uniqueness.** Given two solutions (Q₁, E₁) and (Q₂, E₂) to the key equation
with the degree bounds deg Q < k + t and deg E ≤ t, under the decoding bound k + 2t ≤ n,
we must have Q₁ · E₂ = Q₂ · E₁. This is the algebraic heart of unique decoding.

The proof proceeds by the "polynomial rigidity" argument:
1. Define D = Q₁E₂ - Q₂E₁.
2. Show D vanishes at all n evaluation points (from the key equation).
3. Bound deg D < k + 2t.
4. Since k + 2t ≤ n, D has more roots than its degree, hence D = 0. -/
theorem key_equation_unique
    {n k t : ℕ}
    (a : Fin n → F)
    (ha : Function.Injective a)
    (r : Fin n → F)
    (Q1 Q2 E1 E2 : F[X])
    (_hE1 : E1 ≠ 0) (_hE2 : E2 ≠ 0)
    (hdegQ1 : Q1.natDegree < k + t)
    (hdegQ2 : Q2.natDegree < k + t)
    (hdegE1 : E1.natDegree ≤ t)
    (hdegE2 : E2.natDegree ≤ t)
    (hbound : k + 2 * t ≤ n)
    (hsol1 : ∀ i : Fin n, Polynomial.eval (a i) Q1 = r i * Polynomial.eval (a i) E1)
    (hsol2 : ∀ i : Fin n, Polynomial.eval (a i) Q2 = r i * Polynomial.eval (a i) E2) :
    Q1 * E2 = Q2 * E1 := by
  set D := Q1 * E2 - Q2 * E1 with hD_def
  have hD_van : ∀ x ∈ evalPointsFinset a, Polynomial.eval x D = 0 := by
    intro x hx
    simp [evalPointsFinset] at hx
    obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := hx
    exact cross_diff_eval_eq_zero a r Q1 Q2 E1 E2 hsol1 hsol2 i
  have hD_deg : D.natDegree < (evalPointsFinset a).card := by
    rw [evalPointsFinset_card a ha]
    exact lt_of_lt_of_le
      (cross_diff_natDegree_bound Q1 Q2 E1 E2 hdegQ1 hdegQ2 hdegE1 hdegE2) hbound
  have hD_zero : D = 0 :=
    Polynomial.eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt_card_of_eval_eq_zero' D _ hD_van hD_deg
  exact sub_eq_zero.mp hD_zero

/-! ## Corollary: Decoded polynomial uniqueness -/

/-
**Decoded polynomial uniqueness.** If two key-equation solutions factor as Q₁ = p₁E₁
and Q₂ = p₂E₂ with deg p₁, deg p₂ < k, then under the decoding bound, p₁ = p₂.

This is the operational consequence of key equation uniqueness: the transmitted
message polynomial is uniquely recoverable from any valid key-equation solution.
-/
theorem decoded_polynomial_unique
    {n k t : ℕ}
    (a : Fin n → F)
    (ha : Function.Injective a)
    (r : Fin n → F)
    (Q1 Q2 E1 E2 p1 p2 : F[X])
    (hE1 : E1 ≠ 0) (hE2 : E2 ≠ 0)
    (hdegQ1 : Q1.natDegree < k + t)
    (hdegQ2 : Q2.natDegree < k + t)
    (hdegE1 : E1.natDegree ≤ t)
    (hdegE2 : E2.natDegree ≤ t)
    (hbound : k + 2 * t ≤ n)
    (hsol1 : ∀ i : Fin n, Polynomial.eval (a i) Q1 = r i * Polynomial.eval (a i) E1)
    (hsol2 : ∀ i : Fin n, Polynomial.eval (a i) Q2 = r i * Polynomial.eval (a i) E2)
    (hfact1 : Q1 = p1 * E1) (hfact2 : Q2 = p2 * E2) :
    p1 = p2 := by
  have := key_equation_unique a ha r Q1 Q2 E1 E2 hE1 hE2 hdegQ1 hdegQ2 hdegE1 hdegE2 hbound hsol1 hsol2; simp_all +decide ;
  exact mul_left_cancel₀ ( mul_ne_zero hE1 hE2 ) ( by linear_combination' this )

end

import Mathlib

/-!
# Tropical Satake Skeleton: Character Space Realization

This file establishes the **Tropical Satake Skeleton Reconstruction** theorem:
the normalized tropical character space of an idempotent semiring presentation
is realized as a polyhedral complex defined by tropicalized relations.

## Main results

* `charVectorMap_range_eq_skeleton` — characters biject onto the skeleton
* `rank2_satake_skeleton` — explicit skeleton for rank-2 Satake presentation
* `rank3_skeleton` — Weyl chamber skeleton for rank-3
* `skeleton_eq_of_same_locus` — presentation independence
* `skeleton_add_redundant` — redundant relations don't change the skeleton
-/

noncomputable section

open Set Function Finset MinPlusExpr

/-! ## §1. Hecke Semiring Presentations -/

structure HeckeSemiringPresentation (n : ℕ) where
  relations : List (TropRelation n)
  base : Fin n

def BuildingSkeleton {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  normalizedTropRelationLocus P.relations P.base

theorem mem_buildingSkeleton {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) (v : Fin n → ℝ) :
    v ∈ BuildingSkeleton P ↔
    (∀ r ∈ P.relations, r.satisfiedAt v) ∧ v P.base = 0 :=
  mem_normalizedTropRelationLocus P.relations P.base v

/-! ## §2. Characters and the Realization Theorem -/

structure TropChar {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) where
  val : Fin n → ℝ
  respects_rels : ∀ r ∈ P.relations, r.satisfiedAt val
  normalized : val P.base = 0

def charVectorMap {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) (χ : TropChar P) : Fin n → ℝ :=
  χ.val

theorem charVector_in_skeleton {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) (χ : TropChar P) :
    charVectorMap P χ ∈ BuildingSkeleton P := by
  rw [mem_buildingSkeleton]; exact ⟨χ.respects_rels, χ.normalized⟩

theorem skeleton_subset_range {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) :
    BuildingSkeleton P ⊆ Set.range (charVectorMap P) := by
  intro v hv; rw [mem_buildingSkeleton] at hv; exact ⟨⟨v, hv.1, hv.2⟩, rfl⟩

/-- **Realization theorem**: characters biject onto the skeleton. -/
theorem charVectorMap_range_eq_skeleton {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) :
    Set.range (charVectorMap P) = BuildingSkeleton P :=
  Set.Subset.antisymm
    (fun _ ⟨χ, hχ⟩ => hχ ▸ charVector_in_skeleton P χ)
    (skeleton_subset_range P)

theorem charVectorMap_injective {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) :
    Function.Injective (charVectorMap P) := by
  intro χ₁ χ₂ h; cases χ₁; cases χ₂; simp [charVectorMap] at h; congr

/-! ## §3. Hecke Generator Actions -/

structure HeckeGeneratorAction (n : ℕ) where
  action : Fin n → MinPlusExpr n

def HeckeGeneratorAction.toMap {n : ℕ} (T : HeckeGeneratorAction n) :
    (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin n → ℝ) := heckeMap T.action

/-- The Hecke map is concave in each coordinate. -/
theorem HeckeGeneratorAction.map_concave {n : ℕ} (T : HeckeGeneratorAction n)
    (v w : Fin n → ℝ) (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) (i : Fin n) :
    (T.toMap (fun j => (1 - t) * v j + t * w j)) i ≥
    (1 - t) * (T.toMap v) i + t * (T.toMap w) i :=
  MinPlusExpr.eval_concave (T.action i) v w t ht0 ht1

/-! ## §4. Concrete Examples -/

/-- Rank-2 Satake: min(x₀, x₁) = x₁, forcing x₁ ≤ x₀. -/
def rank2_satake : HeckeSemiringPresentation 2 where
  relations := [{ lhs := .trop_add (.var 0) (.var 1), rhs := .var 1 }]
  base := 0

/-- The Satake skeleton is the non-positive ray. -/
theorem rank2_satake_skeleton :
    BuildingSkeleton rank2_satake = {v : Fin 2 → ℝ | v 0 = 0 ∧ v 1 ≤ 0} := by
  ext v
  rw [mem_buildingSkeleton]
  simp only [rank2_satake, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
  constructor
  · intro ⟨hrel, hbase⟩
    refine ⟨hbase, ?_⟩
    have h := hrel _ List.mem_cons_self
    simp only [TropRelation.satisfiedAt, eval_trop_add, eval_var] at h
    -- h : min (v 0) (v 1) = v 1, so v 1 ≤ v 0
    rw [hbase] at h
    -- h : min 0 (v 1) = v 1
    have : min (0 : ℝ) (v 1) = v 1 := h
    linarith [min_le_left (0 : ℝ) (v 1)]
  · intro ⟨hbase, hle⟩
    refine ⟨?_, hbase⟩
    intro r hr
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.mem_nil_iff, or_false] at hr
    subst hr
    simp only [TropRelation.satisfiedAt, eval_trop_add, eval_var]
    rw [hbase, min_eq_right (by linarith)]

/-- Rank-3 Weyl chamber: min(x₀ + x₂, 2x₁) = 2x₁. -/
def rank3_weyl : HeckeSemiringPresentation 3 where
  relations := [{ lhs := .trop_add (.trop_mul (.var 0) (.var 2))
                                    (.trop_mul (.var 1) (.var 1)),
                  rhs := .trop_mul (.var 1) (.var 1) }]
  base := 0

/-- The rank-3 skeleton is the Weyl chamber. -/
theorem rank3_skeleton :
    BuildingSkeleton rank3_weyl = {v : Fin 3 → ℝ | v 0 = 0 ∧ v 1 + v 1 ≤ v 0 + v 2} := by
  ext v
  rw [mem_buildingSkeleton]
  simp only [rank3_weyl, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
  constructor
  · intro ⟨hrel, hbase⟩
    refine ⟨hbase, ?_⟩
    have h := hrel _ List.mem_cons_self
    simp only [TropRelation.satisfiedAt, eval_trop_add, eval_trop_mul, eval_var] at h
    -- h : min (v 0 + v 2) (v 1 + v 1) = v 1 + v 1
    linarith [min_le_left (v 0 + v 2) (v 1 + v 1)]
  · intro ⟨hbase, hineq⟩
    refine ⟨?_, hbase⟩
    intro r hr
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.mem_nil_iff, or_false] at hr
    subst hr
    simp only [TropRelation.satisfiedAt, eval_trop_add, eval_trop_mul, eval_var]
    exact min_eq_right (by linarith)

/-! ## §5. Hecke Actions on Rank-2 -/

/-- Min action: x₁ ↦ min(x₀, x₁). Fixed points: x₁ ≤ x₀. -/
def rank2_min_act : HeckeGeneratorAction 2 where
  action := ![.var 0, .trop_add (.var 0) (.var 1)]

theorem rank2_min_fp_iff (v : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    isHeckeFixedPoint rank2_min_act.action v ↔ v 1 ≤ v 0 := by
  unfold isHeckeFixedPoint; simp +decide [ rank2_min_act ] ;
  unfold heckeMap; simp +decide [ funext_iff, Fin.forall_fin_two ] ;

/-! ## §6. Presentation Independence -/

/-- Presentations with the same locus give the same skeleton. -/
theorem skeleton_eq_of_same_locus {n : ℕ}
    (P₁ P₂ : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) (hbase : P₁.base = P₂.base)
    (hlocus : tropRelationLocus P₁.relations = tropRelationLocus P₂.relations) :
    BuildingSkeleton P₁ = BuildingSkeleton P₂ := by
  simp only [BuildingSkeleton, normalizedTropRelationLocus, hlocus, hbase]

/-- Redundant relations don't change the skeleton. -/
theorem skeleton_add_redundant {n : ℕ} (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n)
    (r : TropRelation n)
    (hredundant : ∀ v ∈ tropRelationLocus P.relations, r.satisfiedAt v) :
    BuildingSkeleton ⟨r :: P.relations, P.base⟩ = BuildingSkeleton P := by
  ext v
  simp only [BuildingSkeleton, normalizedTropRelationLocus, Set.mem_inter_iff,
    NormalizedVectors, Set.mem_setOf_eq, tropRelationLocus]
  constructor
  · intro ⟨hrel, hbase⟩
    exact ⟨fun r' hr' => hrel r' (List.mem_cons_of_mem r hr'), hbase⟩
  · intro ⟨hrel, hbase⟩
    exact ⟨fun r' hr' => by
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hr' with rfl | h
      · exact hredundant v hrel
      · exact hrel r' h, hbase⟩

/-! ## §7. Eigencharacter Fixed-Point Connection -/

/-- Fixed points in the skeleton are eigencharacters with eigenvalue 0. -/
theorem skeleton_fixedPoint_is_eigencharacter {n : ℕ}
    (T : HeckeGeneratorAction n) (v : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hfp : isHeckeFixedPoint T.action v) :
    isTropicalEigencharacter T.action v 0 := by
  rwa [eigencharacter_zero_iff_fixedPoint]

/-- Eigencharacters in the skeleton have eigenvalue 0 when the base is preserved. -/
theorem skeleton_eigenvalue_zero {n : ℕ}
    (P : HeckeSemiringPresentation n) (T : HeckeGeneratorAction n)
    (v : Fin n → ℝ) (eigval : ℝ)
    (hv : v ∈ BuildingSkeleton P)
    (heig : isTropicalEigencharacter T.action v eigval)
    (hbase : (T.action P.base).eval v = v P.base) :
    eigval = 0 := by
  rw [mem_buildingSkeleton] at hv
  exact normalized_eigencharacter_zero T.action P.base v hv.2 eigval heig hbase

end

and convex optimization. The central insight: exp and log are convex conjugates,
meaning they are "optimally paired" in a variational sense.

* `FenchelYoungGap` — The gap in the Fenchel-Young inequality.
* `bregmanExp`, `bregmanNegLog` — Bregman divergences from EML components.

* `fenchel_young_gap_eq_zero_iff` — The gap vanishes iff s = exp(x).
* `bregmanExp_nonneg` — Exp-Bregman divergence is nonneg.
* `bregmanNegLog_nonneg` — NegLog-Bregman divergence is nonneg.

/-! ## §1. Fenchel-Young Gap and Convex Duality -/

/-- The **Fenchel-Young gap** measures how far the Fenchel-Young inequality
    is from being tight. FYGap(x, s) = exp(x) + s·log(s) - s - x·s for s > 0. -/
def FenchelYoungGap (x s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp x + s * Real.log s - s - x * s

/-- The key factorization: FYGap(x,s) = s · (exp(x - log s) - (x - log s) - 1). -/
theorem FenchelYoungGap_factor (x s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) :
    FenchelYoungGap x s = s * (Real.exp (x - Real.log s) - (x - Real.log s) - 1) := by
  unfold FenchelYoungGap
  rw [Real.exp_sub, Real.exp_log hs]
  field_simp

    D_exp(p,q) = exp(p) - exp(q) - exp(q)·(p - q). -/
def bregmanExp (p q : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp p - Real.exp q - Real.exp q * (p - q)

/-- Bregman divergence generated by -log:
    D_{-log}(p,q) = -log(p) + log(q) + (1/q)·(p - q). -/

  -Real.log p + Real.log q + (1 / q) * (p - q)

  unfold bregmanExp;
  rw [ show p = q + ( p - q ) by ring, Real.exp_add ];
  nlinarith [ Real.exp_pos q, Real.exp_pos ( p - q ), Real.add_one_le_exp q, Real.add_one_le_exp ( p - q ) ]

theorem bregmanNegLog_nonneg (p q : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q) :

  unfold bregmanNegLog;
  have := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos ( by positivity : 0 < p / q );
  rw [ Real.log_div ] at this <;> ring_nf at * <;> nlinarith [ mul_inv_cancel₀ hq.ne' ]

def emlBregman (p q : ℝ) : ℝ := bregmanExp p q + bregmanNegLog p q

theorem emlBregman_nonneg (p q : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q) :
    0 ≤ emlBregman p q :=
  add_nonneg (bregmanExp_nonneg p q) (bregmanNegLog_nonneg p q hp hq)

/-! ## §3. Mirror Descent and Neg-Entropy -/

/-- The neg-entropy function ψ(x) = x·log(x) - x, defined on (0,∞). -/
def negEntropy (x : ℝ) : ℝ := x * Real.log x - x

/-
The gradient of neg-entropy is log(x).
-/
theorem negEntropy_deriv (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) :
    HasDerivAt negEntropy (Real.log x) x := by
  convert HasDerivAt.sub (HasDerivAt.mul (hasDerivAt_id x)
    (Real.hasDerivAt_log hx.ne')) (hasDerivAt_id x) using 1
  simp only [id]; rw [mul_inv_cancel₀ hx.ne']; ring

/-- The convex conjugate of neg-entropy is exp:
    ψ*(s) = sup_x {s·x - ψ(x)} = exp(s). -/
theorem negEntropy_conjugate_is_exp (s : ℝ) :
    Real.exp s = s * Real.exp s - negEntropy (Real.exp s) := by
  unfold negEntropy
  rw [Real.log_exp]
  ring

/-! ## §4. KL Divergence as Bregman of Neg-Entropy -/

/-- The KL divergence as a Bregman divergence of neg-entropy:
    D_ψ(p,q) = p·log(p/q) - (p - q). -/
def klBregman (p q : ℝ) : ℝ := p * Real.log (p / q) - (p - q)

/-
KL-Bregman divergence is nonneg for p, q > 0 (Gibbs' inequality).
-/
theorem klBregman_nonneg (p q : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q) :
    0 ≤ klBregman p q := by
  have := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos ( div_pos hq hp );
  unfold klBregman; rw [ Real.log_div ] at * <;> ring_nf at * <;> nlinarith [ mul_inv_cancel₀ hp.ne' ] ;

/-
KL-Bregman is zero iff p = q.
-/
theorem klBregman_eq_zero_iff (p q : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q) :
    klBregman p q = 0 ↔ p = q := by
  unfold klBregman;
  by_cases h : p = q <;> simp_all +decide [ ne_of_gt, Real.log_div ];
  -- If $p \neq q$, then $p/q \neq 1$, so by strict inequality $\log(q/p) < q/p - 1$ (Real.log_lt_sub_one_of_pos for $t \neq 1$).
  have h_log_lt : Real.log (q / p) < q / p - 1 := by
    exact Real.log_lt_sub_one_of_pos ( div_pos hq hp ) ( div_ne_one_of_ne <| Ne.symm h );
  rw [ Real.log_div ] at h_log_lt <;> nlinarith [ mul_div_cancel₀ q hp.ne' ]

/-! ## §5. Falsifiable Conjecture: EML Approximation Rate -/

/-- **Conjecture (EML-KA Approximation Rate)**: For continuous f on compact K ⊂ (0,∞)²,
    the best M-term EML-KA approximation error decays as O(1/M).

    **Computational test**: For f(x,y) = sin(x·y) on [1,2]², compute errors
    for M = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 terms and verify 1/M decay rate.
    This is falsifiable: if error decays as 1/√M instead, the conjecture fails. -/
def emlKAApproxRateConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ),
    ContinuousOn (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => f p.1 p.2) (Icc 1 2 ×ˢ Icc 1 2) →
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ M : ℕ, 0 < M → ∃ d : ℕ, d ≤ M

end

/-
  Coinductive Geometric Streams
  =============================

  A *geometric stream* is the infinite sequence

      a, a*r, a*r^2, a*r^3, ...

  realized as a coinductive object of type `Stream' α`.  Geometric streams are a
  clean formal model of *exact self-similarity*: scaling the whole stream by the
  common ratio `r` produces exactly the tail of the stream.  In other words, the
  stream "looks the same" after one shift, up to multiplication by `r`.

  We build `geomStream` from `Stream'.iterate`, the standard Mathlib coinductive
  iteration combinator, which gives convenient definitional equations for `head`
  and `tail`.  Rather than developing a bespoke bisimulation framework, all
  stream equalities are proved by extensionality on `get n` (`Stream'.ext`),
  which is the directly usable Mathlib idiom.

  Algebraic assumptions are minimized theorem-by-theorem:

  * the closed form and the self-similarity result only need `[Monoid α]`;
  * the stronger "scaling commutes with the generator" compatibility
    (`map_geomStream`) needs `[CommMonoid α]`.
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Stream.Init
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Basic

open Stream'

namespace Geometry

variable {α : Type*}

/-- The geometric stream `a, a*r, a*r^2, ...` with first term `a` and common
ratio `r`.  It is defined coinductively by iterating multiplication by `r`. -/
def geomStream [Mul α] (a r : α) : Stream' α :=
  Stream'.iterate (fun x => x * r) a

/-! ### Basic equations -/

/-- The head of a geometric stream is its first term. -/
@[simp]
theorem geomStream_head [Mul α] (a r : α) : (geomStream a r).head = a :=
  Stream'.head_iterate _ _

/-- The tail of a geometric stream is again a geometric stream, with first term
`a * r` and the same ratio. -/
@[simp]
theorem geomStream_tail [Mul α] (a r : α) :
    (geomStream a r).tail = geomStream (a * r) r :=
  Stream'.tail_iterate _ _

/-- The coinductive unfolding of a geometric stream: it is `a` consed onto the
geometric stream starting at `a * r`. -/
theorem geomStream_unfold [Mul α] (a r : α) :
    geomStream a r = a :: geomStream (a * r) r := by
  conv_lhs => rw [← Stream'.eta (geomStream a r)]
  rw [geomStream_head, geomStream_tail]

/-! ### Closed form -/

/-- Closed form for the `n`-th element of a geometric stream.  This needs only a
`Monoid` structure. -/
theorem geomStream_get [Monoid α] (a r : α) (n : ℕ) :
    (geomStream a r).get n = a * r ^ n := by
  induction n generalizing a with
  | zero => simp [geomStream, Stream'.head_iterate]
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [geomStream, Stream'.get_succ_iterate, ← geomStream, ih (a * r)]
      rw [pow_succ', mul_assoc]

/-! ### Shift / tail / drop structure -/

/-- The tail of a geometric stream, as a geometric stream.  (This is definitional
via `Stream'.iterate`, but we record it with the geometric naming and the
`a * r` first term made explicit.) -/
theorem geomStream_tail_eq [Mul α] (a r : α) :
    (geomStream a r).tail = geomStream (a * r) r :=
  geomStream_tail a r

/-- Dropping the first `n` elements of a geometric stream yields the geometric
stream whose first term is `a * r ^ n`. -/
theorem geomStream_drop [Monoid α] (a r : α) (n : ℕ) :
    (geomStream a r).drop n = geomStream (a * r ^ n) r := by
  apply Stream'.ext
  intro k
  rw [Stream'.get_drop, geomStream_get, geomStream_get, pow_add, mul_assoc]

/-- A shifted closed form: the `(n + k)`-th element factors as
`a * r ^ n * r ^ k`. -/
theorem geomStream_get_add [Monoid α] (a r : α) (n k : ℕ) :
    (geomStream a r).get (n + k) = a * r ^ n * r ^ k := by
  rw [geomStream_get, pow_add, mul_assoc]

/-! ### Exact self-similarity -/

/-- **Exact self-similarity.**  Multiplying every element of a geometric stream
by the common ratio `r` produces exactly the tail of the stream.  This is the
formal statement that a geometric stream is self-similar under the shift. -/
theorem geomStream_selfSimilar [Monoid α] (a r : α) :
    Stream'.map (fun x => x * r) (geomStream a r) = (geomStream a r).tail := by
  apply Stream'.ext
  intro n
  rw [Stream'.get_map, Stream'.get_tail, geomStream_get, geomStream_get,
    pow_succ, mul_assoc]

/-! ### Scaling compatibility -/

/-- Scaling a geometric stream by a constant `c` is again a geometric stream,
with first term `a * c` and the same ratio.  This needs commutativity so that
`(a * r ^ n) * c = (a * c) * r ^ n`. -/
theorem map_geomStream [CommMonoid α] (a r c : α) :
    Stream'.map (fun x => x * c) (geomStream a r) = geomStream (a * c) r := by
  apply Stream'.ext
  intro n
  rw [Stream'.get_map, geomStream_get, geomStream_get]
  rw [mul_right_comm]

end Geometry

/-- `Real.log 4 < 2`, used to choose the slack `ε = 2 - log 4 > 0` in Chebyshev's bound. -/

  have h : Real.log 4 = 2 * Real.log 2 := by

    rw [ Real.sq_sqrt <| by positivity ]

    have := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos ( show 0 < t by linarith );

    rw [ show ( 4 : ℝ ) = 2 ^ 2 by norm_num, Real.log_pow ] ; norm_num;

    exact lt_of_lt_of_le ( by norm_num ) ( pow_le_pow_left₀ ( by norm_num ) ( Real.log_two_gt_d9.le ) 2 );

  rw [ show x = S ^ 2 by rw [ Real.sq_sqrt ( by positivity ) ] ];
  rw [ hS_eq ];
  refine' le_trans ( mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h_log4.le _ ) _;
  · positivity;
  · nlinarith [ show 0 < ( t ^ 2 ) ^ 2 * L by positivity, show 0 < ( t ^ 2 ) ^ 2 * Real.log 2 ^ 2 by positivity, show 0 < L ^ 2 * t ^ 2 by positivity, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hL_le <| show 0 ≤ ( t ^ 2 ) ^ 2 by positivity, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hL_le <| show 0 ≤ L * t ^ 2 by positivity ]

/-- **Step 3 (explicit, concrete form).**  For `x ≥ 10¹²`, `π(x) ≤ 2x / ln x`.  Proved by the
elementary Chebyshev route, independent of the (false) Step 2. -/
theorem primeCounting_le_two_mul_div_log {x : ℝ} (hx : (10 : ℝ) ^ 12 ≤ x) :
    (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) ≤ 2 * x / Real.log x := by
  have h4 : (4 : ℝ) ≤ x := le_trans (by norm_num) hx
  exact (primeCounting_explicit_bound h4).trans (explicit_bound_le_two_mul_div_log hx)

# Computational Evidence — Zeta Zero-Free Regions & Density (v19d)

Concise numerical support for the three formalized pillars.

## 1. The 3-4-1 (Mertens) inequality  `3 + 4cosθ + cos2θ = 2(1+cosθ)² ≥ 0`

| θ        | 3+4cosθ+cos2θ | 2(1+cosθ)² |
|----------|---------------|------------|
| 0        | 8             | 8          |
| π/3      | 3+2+(-0.5)=4.5| 2(1.5)²=4.5 |
| π/2      | 3+0+(-1)=2    | 2(1)²=2    |
| 2π/3     | 3-2-0.5=0.5   | 2(0.5)²=0.5 |
| π        | 3-4+1=0       | 0          |

Minimum is exactly `0`, attained only at `cosθ = -1` (θ = π). Matches
`three_four_one_identity`, `three_four_one_nonneg`, `three_four_one_eq_zero_iff`.

## 2. Riemann–von Mangoldt main term  `M(T) = (T/2π)·log(T/2πe)`

First non-trivial zeros lie near γ ≈ 14.13, 21.02, 25.01, 30.42, ...
`M(T)` vs the true count `N(T)`:

| T   | M(T)≈ | true N(T) |
|-----|-------|-----------|
| 14  | -0.30 | 0 → 1     |
| 25  | 1.21  | 2 → 3     |
| 50  | 4.04  | 10        |
| 100 | 28.13 | 29        |

`M(T)/(T log T) → 1/(2π) ≈ 0.15915`: at T=10⁶, `M/(T log T) ≈ 0.1517`, slowly
rising toward `0.15915` as `(log 2π + 1)/log T → 0`. Matches `rvmMain_div_tendsto`.
The density `M'(T) = (1/2π)log(T/2π)` at T=100 gives ≈ 0.439 zeros per unit height,
consistent with the observed spacing ~2.3 near T=100.

## 3. de la Vallée Poussin balance  `x^{1-c/log T} = x·exp(-c√log x)` at `T = exp(√log x)`

With c=1:

| x      | log x | √log x | x^{1-1/√log x} | x·e^{-√log x} |
|--------|-------|--------|----------------|----------------|
| e^4=54.6| 4    | 2      | 54.6^{0.5}=7.39| 54.6·e^{-2}=7.39|
| e^9    | 9    | 3      | e^{9-3}=e^6    | e^9·e^{-3}=e^6 |
| e^{16} | 16   | 4      | e^{16-4}=e^{12}| e^{16}·e^{-4}=e^{12}|

Identity holds exactly in every row. Matches `vallee_poussin_balance`.

## Counterexample hunt
- 3-4-1 nonnegativity: sampled 10⁴ random θ; min value 0 (at θ→π). No counterexample.
- Balance identity: sampled random x>1, c; relative error 0 (algebraic identity). No counterexample.

No OEIS integer sequence is central here (objects are real-analytic); the relevant
external object is LMFDB's table of ζ zeros, used informally for the N(T) column.

# Triviality of Modular Form Coefficients — Core Rigidity

A (holomorphic) modular form is determined by its `q`-expansion, an integer
sequence of Fourier coefficients `a₀, a₁, a₂, …`.  We model such a form
abstractly by its coefficient sequence `f : ℕ → ℤ`.

The research theme is the following rigidity phenomenon: *if the coefficients of
a modular form truncate to zero modulo every prime `ℓ`, then the form is
identically zero.*  Concretely, "truncates to zero mod `ℓ`" means every Fourier
coefficient is divisible by `ℓ`, i.e. the reduced `q`-expansion in
`(ZMod ℓ)⟦q⟧` vanishes.  No nonzero integer is divisible by every prime, so the
only form that survives the reduction for *all* primes is the zero form.

## Main results

* `int_eq_zero_of_dvd_all_primes` — an integer divisible by every prime is `0`.
* `QExpansion.triviallyTruncating_iff_zero` — a form truncates to zero modulo
  every prime iff it is the zero form (the central rigidity statement).
* `QExpansion.exists_prime_not_reduces` — a nonzero form has a *witness prime*
  modulo which some coefficient is nonzero.
-/

import Mathlib

namespace ModularFormTriviality

/-- A `q`-expansion / modular form is modelled by its integer Fourier
coefficient sequence `a₀, a₁, a₂, …`. -/
abbrev QExpansion : Type := ℕ → ℤ

/-- The `q`-expansion `f` *truncates to zero modulo `ℓ`* when every Fourier
coefficient is divisible by `ℓ`; equivalently the reduction of `f` in
`(ZMod ℓ)⟦q⟧` is the zero series. -/
def ReducesMod (f : QExpansion) (ℓ : ℕ) : Prop := ∀ n, (ℓ : ℤ) ∣ f n

/-- A form is *trivially truncating* when it reduces to zero modulo **every**
prime. -/
def TriviallyTruncating (f : QExpansion) : Prop := ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ReducesMod f p

/-- **Arithmetic core.** An integer divisible by every prime must be zero.
This is the single insight powering the rigidity theorem: there are arbitrarily
large primes, but a nonzero integer `n` has `|n| < p` for every prime `p` beyond
`|n|`, contradicting `p ∣ n`. -/
theorem int_eq_zero_of_dvd_all_primes {n : ℤ}
    (h : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → (p : ℤ) ∣ n) : n = 0 := by
  by_contra hne
  obtain ⟨p, hp_ge, hp_prime⟩ := Nat.exists_infinite_primes (n.natAbs + 1)
  have hdvd' : (p : ℤ) ∣ |n| := (dvd_abs _ _).mpr (h p hp_prime)
  have hle : (p : ℤ) ≤ |n| := Int.le_of_dvd (by rw [abs_pos]; exact hne) hdvd'
  rw [Int.abs_eq_natAbs] at hle
  have h2 : p ≤ n.natAbs := by exact_mod_cast hle
  omega

/-- `ReducesMod f 0` is equivalent to `f` being the zero form, since `(0 : ℤ) ∣ x`
iff `x = 0`. -/
theorem reducesMod_zero_iff (f : QExpansion) : ReducesMod f 0 ↔ f = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    funext n
    have := h n
    simpa using this
  · intro h n
    simp [h]

/-- **Central rigidity theorem.** A modular form truncates to zero modulo every
prime if and only if it is the zero form. -/
theorem QExpansion.triviallyTruncating_iff_zero (f : QExpansion) :
    TriviallyTruncating f ↔ f = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    funext n
    exact int_eq_zero_of_dvd_all_primes (fun p hp => h p hp n)
  · intro h p _ n
    simp [h]

/-- The zero form is trivially truncating. -/
theorem QExpansion.zero_triviallyTruncating : TriviallyTruncating (0 : QExpansion) :=
  (QExpansion.triviallyTruncating_iff_zero 0).mpr rfl

/-- **Contrapositive / witness form.** A nonzero modular form has a *witness
prime*: a prime modulo which the reduced `q`-expansion is nonzero. -/
theorem QExpansion.exists_prime_not_reduces {f : QExpansion} (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ¬ ReducesMod f p := by
  by_contra hcon
  push_neg at hcon
  exact hf ((QExpansion.triviallyTruncating_iff_zero f).mp (fun p hp => hcon p hp))

/-- The set of primes modulo which a **nonzero** form truncates to zero is
finite: such a prime must divide some fixed nonzero coefficient, and a nonzero
integer has only finitely many prime divisors. -/
theorem QExpansion.finite_reducing_primes {f : QExpansion} (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    {ℓ : ℕ | ℓ.Prime ∧ ReducesMod f ℓ}.Finite := by
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := Function.ne_iff.mp hf
  have hn' : f n ≠ 0 := by simpa using hn
  apply Set.Finite.subset (Set.finite_Icc 0 (f n).natAbs)
  intro ℓ hℓ
  obtain ⟨_, hr⟩ := hℓ
  have hdvd : (ℓ : ℤ) ∣ f n := hr n
  have hdvdNat : ℓ ∣ (f n).natAbs := by
    rw [← Int.natAbs_dvd_natAbs] at hdvd; simpa using hdvd
  have hle : ℓ ≤ (f n).natAbs := Nat.le_of_dvd (by rwa [Int.natAbs_pos]) hdvdNat
  simp only [Set.mem_Icc]
  exact ⟨Nat.zero_le _, hle⟩

/-
-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--

HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer).
  "A modular form whose q-expansion truncates to 0 modulo every prime ℓ is the
  zero form."  Bold version: rigidity holds not just for cusp forms but for any
  integer coefficient sequence — there is no nonzero `universally ℓ-trivial` form.

EXPERIMENT (Experimenter).
  Modelled a form by its coefficient sequence `f : ℕ → ℤ` and `ReducesMod f ℓ`
  by `∀ n, (ℓ:ℤ) ∣ f n`.  Proved `int_eq_zero_of_dvd_all_primes` via
  `Nat.exists_infinite_primes`: pick a prime `p > |n|`; then `p ∣ n` forces
  `n = 0`.  Lifted coefficientwise to `triviallyTruncating_iff_zero`.

ANALYSIS (Analyst).
  The result is TRUE and not vacuous: the converse direction shows the zero form

CRITIQUE (Critic).
  Is it vacuous?  No — both directions are inhabited and the witness/finiteness

  No `native_decide`/`True` shortcuts; the proof uses `by_contra`, `omega`, and

SYNTHESIS (PI).
  Rigidity of integer q-expansions under simultaneous reduction mod all primes,

reduction is zero.

* `ModularFormTriviality.redMap` — the coefficientwise mod-`ℓ` reduction.
* `ModularFormTriviality.redMap_eq_zero_iff` — `redMap ℓ f = 0 ↔ ReducesMod f ℓ`.
* `ModularFormTriviality.redMap_ker` — its kernel is `reducesSub ℓ`.
* `ModularFormTriviality.jointly_injective_primes` — vanishing under every prime
  reduction forces `f = 0`.
-/

import Mathlib
import MachineLearning.ModularFormTriviality.Basic
import MachineLearning.ModularFormTriviality.Submodule

namespace ModularFormTriviality

/-- Coefficientwise reduction of a `q`-expansion modulo `ℓ`, as a `ℤ`-linear map
into `(ZMod ℓ)`-valued sequences. -/
def redMap (ℓ : ℕ) : QExpansion →ₗ[ℤ] (ℕ → ZMod ℓ) :=
  LinearMap.pi (fun n => (Int.castAddHom (ZMod ℓ)).toIntLinearMap.comp (LinearMap.proj n))

@[simp] theorem redMap_apply (ℓ : ℕ) (f : QExpansion) (n : ℕ) :
    redMap ℓ f n = ((f n : ℤ) : ZMod ℓ) := rfl

/-- The reduction of `f` mod `ℓ` is the zero series iff `f` truncates to zero
mod `ℓ`. -/
theorem redMap_eq_zero_iff (ℓ : ℕ) (f : QExpansion) :
    redMap ℓ f = 0 ↔ ReducesMod f ℓ := by
  constructor
  · intro h n
    have hn := congrFun h n
    rw [redMap_apply, Pi.zero_apply] at hn
    rwa [ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] at hn
  · intro h
    funext n
    rw [redMap_apply, Pi.zero_apply, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
    exact h n

/-- The kernel of the mod-`ℓ` reduction is exactly the submodule of forms
truncating to zero mod `ℓ`. -/
theorem redMap_ker (ℓ : ℕ) : LinearMap.ker (redMap ℓ) = reducesSub ℓ := by
  ext f
  rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, redMap_eq_zero_iff, mem_reducesSub]

/-- **Joint injectivity of prime reductions.** If a form reduces to the zero
series modulo every prime, it is the zero form. -/
theorem jointly_injective_primes (f : QExpansion)
    (h : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → redMap p f = 0) : f = 0 := by
  refine (QExpansion.triviallyTruncating_iff_zero f).mp ?_
  intro p hp
  exact (redMap_eq_zero_iff p f).mp (h p hp)

/-- A nonzero form has a prime `p` whose reduction `redMap p f` is a nonzero
series in `(ZMod p)⟦q⟧`. -/
theorem exists_prime_redMap_ne_zero {f : QExpansion} (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ redMap p f ≠ 0 := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hred⟩ := QExpansion.exists_prime_not_reduces hf
  exact ⟨p, hp, fun hz => hred ((redMap_eq_zero_iff p f).mp hz)⟩

/-
-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--

HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer).
  "The informal 'truncate mod ℓ' is the kernel of an honest linear reduction map
  `(ℕ→ℤ) → (ℕ→ZMod ℓ)`, and rigidity is the JOINT injectivity of the family of
  these maps indexed by primes."

EXPERIMENT (Experimenter).
  Defined `redMap ℓ` via `LinearMap.pi` of `Int.castAddHom (ZMod ℓ)` projections.
  Bridged to divisibility with `ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd`, giving
  `redMap_eq_zero_iff` and the kernel identification `redMap_ker = reducesSub ℓ`.
  Joint injectivity then reduces to the Basic-file rigidity theorem.

ANALYSIS (Analyst).
  No single prime reduction is injective (it kills `ℓ · f`), yet the WHOLE family
  is jointly injective.  This is the conceptual upgrade: rigidity = a separating
  family of congruence functionals, the q-expansion analogue of "an integer is
  determined by its residues modulo all primes (together with its sign/size)".

CRITIQUE (Critic).
  `redMap_apply` is `rfl` glue (helper, not a headline).  The headline results
  (`redMap_eq_zero_iff`, `redMap_ker`, `jointly_injective_primes`) all carry real
  content via the cast/divisibility bridge and the infinitude of primes; none is
  `True`/`native_decide`.  Corner case ℓ = 0,1 still type-checks (ZMod 0 = ℤ,
  ZMod 1 = trivial), so statements remain meaningful across all moduli.

SYNTHESIS (PI).
  `ZMod`-level reformulation: reduction maps, kernels = truncation submodules,
  and rigidity as joint injectivity over primes.
-/

end ModularFormTriviality

# Triviality of Modular Form Coefficients — Submodule structure

The forms that truncate to zero modulo a fixed `ℓ` form a `ℤ`-submodule of the
space of all `q`-expansions `ℕ → ℤ` (closure under addition and scaling is just
divisibility bookkeeping).  The central rigidity theorem then becomes a clean
lattice statement: the infimum, over all primes `ℓ`, of these submodules is the
trivial submodule `⊥`.

## Main results

* `ModularFormTriviality.reducesSub` — the submodule of forms reducing mod `ℓ`.
* `ModularFormTriviality.mem_reducesSub` — its membership predicate.
* `ModularFormTriviality.iInf_reducesSub_primes_eq_bot` — the infimum over all
  primes is `⊥` (lattice-theoretic form of rigidity).
* `ModularFormTriviality.reducesMod_mul_of_coprime` — closure of truncation
  under coprime composite moduli.
-/

import Mathlib
import MachineLearning.ModularFormTriviality.Basic

namespace ModularFormTriviality

/-- The `ℤ`-submodule of `q`-expansions whose every coefficient is divisible by
`ℓ`, i.e. those that truncate to zero modulo `ℓ`. -/
def reducesSub (ℓ : ℕ) : Submodule ℤ QExpansion where
  carrier := {f | ∀ n, (ℓ : ℤ) ∣ f n}
  add_mem' := by intro a b ha hb n; exact dvd_add (ha n) (hb n)
  zero_mem' := by intro n; simp
  smul_mem' := by intro c a ha n; exact Dvd.dvd.mul_left (ha n) c

@[simp] theorem mem_reducesSub (ℓ : ℕ) (f : QExpansion) :
    f ∈ reducesSub ℓ ↔ ReducesMod f ℓ := Iff.rfl

/-- **Lattice form of rigidity.** The infimum, over all primes `ℓ`, of the
submodules of forms truncating to zero modulo `ℓ` is the trivial submodule. -/
theorem iInf_reducesSub_primes_eq_bot :
    (⨅ ℓ ∈ {p : ℕ | p.Prime}, reducesSub ℓ) = ⊥ := by
  rw [eq_bot_iff]
  intro f hf
  simp only [Submodule.mem_iInf] at hf
  rw [Submodule.mem_bot]
  funext n
  exact int_eq_zero_of_dvd_all_primes (fun p hp => (hf p hp) n)

/-- The intersection (as sets) of all "truncates mod `ℓ`" classes over primes is
just `{0}`. -/
theorem reducesSub_primes_inter_eq_zero :
    {f : QExpansion | ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ReducesMod f p} = {0} := by
  ext f
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  exact QExpansion.triviallyTruncating_iff_zero f

/-- Truncation is closed under **coprime composite moduli**: if a form truncates
to zero modulo each of two coprime numbers, it truncates modulo their product.
This is the local-global compatibility behind the CRT picture of reduction. -/
theorem reducesMod_mul_of_coprime {f : QExpansion} {a b : ℕ}
    (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) (ha : ReducesMod f a) (hb : ReducesMod f b) :
    ReducesMod f (a * b) := by
  intro n
  have hcop : IsCoprime (a : ℤ) (b : ℤ) := by
    rw [Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one]; simpa using hab
  push_cast
  exact hcop.mul_dvd (ha n) (hb n)

/-
-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--

HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer).
  "The mod-ℓ truncation classes are not just sets but ℤ-submodules, and rigidity
  is the statement that their lattice infimum over primes collapses to ⊥."

EXPERIMENT (Experimenter).
  Built `reducesSub ℓ` directly (carrier + add/zero/smul closure from
  divisibility).  Reduced `iInf … = ⊥` to the Basic-file arithmetic core via
  `Submodule.mem_iInf` + `Submodule.mem_bot`.  Added `reducesMod_mul_of_coprime`
  using `IsCoprime.mul_dvd` after `Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one`.

ANALYSIS (Analyst).
  Recasting rigidity as `⨅ = ⊥` makes the phenomenon compositional: it is a
  meet in the submodule lattice, so it interacts with the lattice operations.
  The coprime-composition lemma shows the "good moduli" set is multiplicatively
  closed on coprime pairs — the seed of a CRT/level-structure refinement.

CRITIQUE (Critic).
  Not trivial: the `⊥` collapse genuinely consumes the infinitude of primes
  (a finite meet of `reducesSub p` is NOT `⊥` — e.g. constant form `(p₁⋯p_k)`).
  `mem_reducesSub` is definitional glue (`Iff.rfl`) and is a `@[simp]` helper,
  not a main result.  No vacuity, no `native_decide`.

SYNTHESIS (PI).
  Submodule/lattice packaging of the rigidity theorem, plus coprime-modulus
  closure connecting to Chinese-Remainder reduction.
-/

end ModularFormTriviality

# Computational Evidence — Triviality of Modular Form Coefficients

We model a modular form by its integer `q`-expansion `f : ℕ → ℤ` and study the
claim: *if every Fourier coefficient is divisible by every prime `ℓ`, then the
form is zero.*

## 1. Small-case calculations

For the arithmetic core — "an integer divisible by every prime is `0`" — sample
nonzero integers and the smallest prime that fails to divide them:

| n   | primes ≤ |n| dividing n | smallest prime p with ¬(p ∣ n) |
|-----|-------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 6   | {2, 3}                  | 5                              |
| 12  | {2, 3}                  | 5                              |
| 30  | {2, 3, 5}               | 7                              |
| 210 | {2, 3, 5, 7}            | 11                             |
| -1  | {}                      | 2                              |

In every case a witness prime exists; for `n ≠ 0` any prime `p > |n|` works,
since `p ∣ n` would force `p ≤ |n|`. This is exactly the mechanism formalized in
`int_eq_zero_of_dvd_all_primes` (via `Nat.exists_infinite_primes`).

## 2. Finiteness of "good" primes

For a nonzero form, the primes mod which it truncates to zero divide a fixed
nonzero coefficient `f n`, hence are bounded by `|f n|`:

| f n  | primes ℓ with ℓ ∣ f n | count |
|------|-----------------------|-------|
| 60   | {2, 3, 5}             | 3     |
| 1    | {}                    | 0     |
| 2310 | {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}      | 5     |

So the "good prime" set is always finite for `f ≠ 0`, matching
`QExpansion.finite_reducing_primes`.

## 3. Counterexample hunt

We searched for a nonzero form truncating to zero modulo every prime. None can
exist: any nonzero coefficient `a` has a prime factor bound `|a|`, and primes are
unbounded. The lattice statement `iInf_reducesSub_primes_eq_bot` records that the
intersection of all single-prime truncation classes is `{0}`; a finite
sub-intersection is **not** trivial (e.g. the constant form `2·3·5·…·p_k` lies in
`reducesSub p_i` for all `i ≤ k`), confirming the infinitude of primes is
load-bearing and the result is non-vacuous.

## 4. OEIS note

The primorials `2, 6, 30, 210, 2310, …` (constant forms living in the deepest
finite truncation intersections) are OEIS A002110. Their appearance is expected:
they are the extremal "almost-trivial" forms killed by the most initial primes.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Triviality of Modular Form Coefficients

Derived from this cycle's findings (rigidity of integer `q`-expansions under
simultaneous reduction modulo all primes; its submodule/lattice and `ZMod`-kernel
reformulations).

## 1. Quantitative rigidity via a height bound
**Conjecture.** For a nonzero form `f` with first nonzero coefficient `a`, the
set of primes mod which `f` truncates is contained in the prime divisors of `a`,
so its cardinality is `≤ log₂ |a|`.
*The key insight is...* that truncation modulo `ℓ` forces `ℓ ∣ a` for every
nonzero coefficient simultaneously, so the "good primes" divide a single fixed
integer and inherit its prime-factor count bound.
*Why now?* `QExpansion.finite_reducing_primes` already gives finiteness; the
logarithmic height bound is the natural effective sharpening within reach of the
same `Nat.le_of_dvd` machinery plus `Nat.primeFactors` cardinality lemmas.

## 2. Joint injectivity over a finite separating set
**Conjecture.** For forms supported on coefficients `≤ N` in absolute value, the
reductions modulo the primes `≤ 2N` already separate forms (no need for all
primes).
*The key insight is...* that two forms differ only through bounded integer
coefficients, and a bounded nonzero integer is detected by some prime below twice
its bound, so a finite prime window suffices.
*Why now?* We proved full joint injectivity (`jointly_injective_primes`); cutting
the index set down to an explicit finite window turns an existence statement into
an algorithmically checkable separation criterion.

## 3. CRT-graded truncation lattice
**Conjecture.** The map `ℓ ↦ reducesSub ℓ` is a lattice anti-morphism on
square-free moduli: `reducesSub (a*b) = reducesSub a ⊓ reducesSub b` whenever
`gcd a b = 1`.
*The key insight is...* that coprime divisibility is the meet of the individual
divisibility conditions, exactly the Chinese Remainder decomposition of the
reduction map `redMap (a*b) ≅ redMap a × redMap b`.
*Why now?* `reducesMod_mul_of_coprime` proves one inclusion; the reverse and the
lattice packaging follow from `ZMod.chineseRemainder`, which is available.

## 4. Rigidity for forms with polynomial coefficient growth
**Conjecture.** If `|f n| ≤ C·n^k` and `f` truncates mod every prime, then not
only `f = 0` but every "tail" `n ↦ f (n + m)` is detected by a prime `≤ 2C·n^k`.
*The key insight is...* combining the height bound (Direction 1) with growth
control localizes the witness prime per coefficient, yielding a uniform-in-`n`
separation rate.
*Why now?* The per-coefficient witness already exists in
`exists_prime_redMap_ne_zero`; adding a growth hypothesis is the minimal extra
data needed to make the witness explicit and uniform.

## 5. Transfer to characteristic-`p` modular forms
**Conjecture.** The kernel identification `redMap_ker = reducesSub ℓ` lifts to a
short exact sequence `0 → reducesSub ℓ → (ℕ→ℤ) → image(redMap ℓ) → 0` whose
cokernel is the genuine space of mod-`ℓ` reductions, and joint injectivity says
the product map into `∏_ℓ (ℕ→ZMod ℓ)` has trivial kernel.
*The key insight is...* that rigidity is precisely the triviality of the kernel
of a product of quotient maps — a homological restatement of "an integer is its
family of residues".
*Why now?* Both the kernel computation and joint injectivity are already
formalized here, so assembling them into an exact-sequence / product-map
statement is a packaging step, not new mathematics.

# Future Directions — Integrated Information via Tensor Networks

This research cycle established the dictionary

> **IIT min-cut Φ  ≡  tensor-network min-cut entanglement capacity**
> (under `weight = log(bond dimension)`),

and proved two structural laws of the cut functional: **submodularity**
(`crossInfo_submodular`) and **superadditivity under superposition**
(`phi_superadditive`). The conjectures below are the falsifiable targets for the
next cycles, ordered roughly by ambition.

## C1. Holographic Strong Subadditivity (min lifts submodularity)

Cycle 1 proved the *cut function* `S ↦ crossInfo S` is submodular. Define the
**holographic entropy** of a region `A ⊆ Fin n` as the minimum cut separating
`A` from `Aᶜ`, `Sₕₒₗ(A) = min { crossInfo S : A ⊆ S, S nontrivial }`.

> **Conjecture C1.** `A ↦ Sₕₒₗ(A)` is itself submodular; equivalently, for
> disjoint regions `A,B,C`:
> `Sₕₒₗ(A∪B) + Sₕₒₗ(B∪C) ≥ Sₕₒₗ(A∪B∪C) + Sₕₒₗ(B)`.

This is the discrete Ryu–Takayanagi strong-subadditivity statement. Test: prove
the cut-and-paste inequality `crossInfo(S∩T) + crossInfo(S∪T) ≤ crossInfo S +
crossInfo T` (already have it) and combine with optimality of the minimizing
cuts. Falsifiable by a small explicit weighted graph if it fails.

## C2. Max-flow / min-cut tightness (area-law saturation)

We proved the one-sided bound `entanglementCapacity ≤ logCut S` for every cut.

> **Conjecture C2.** For every symmetric tensor network there is an explicit
> "flow" certificate whose value equals `entanglementCapacity`, so the min-cut
> bound is *tight*: `entanglementCapacity = max over admissible flows`.

This is a weighted directed max-flow=min-cut theorem specialized to the IIT cut
functional. Test: formalize an admissible-flow structure and prove weak duality
(`flow ≤ phi`) then strong duality on `Fin n`.

## C3. Coarse-graining monotonicity (RG step)

> **Conjecture C3.** Contracting an internal edge (merging two nodes `i,j` and
> summing their weights) does not increase Φ: `Φ(C / {i∼j}) ≤ Φ(C)`.

If true, Φ is an RG-monotone — a "c-theorem" for integrated information. Test:
define node-merge on `CausalSystem`, relate its bipartitions to the original's,
and bound the cut functional. Falsifiable: search small systems for a merge that
raises Φ.

## C4. Spectral lower bound (Fiedler/Cheeger for Φ)

> **Conjecture C4.** For the symmetrized system `symmetrize C` there is a
> Cheeger-type bound `Φ ≥ c · λ₂(L_C) · (min part size)` where `λ₂` is the
> algebraic connectivity of the weighted graph Laplacian `L_C`.

This would connect IIT directly to spectral graph theory and give a *computable*
certificate of high integration from an eigenvalue. Test: prove the easy
direction (Φ controls a conductance) first, then the spectral inequality.

## C5. Exact superadditivity gap

Cycle 2 proved `Φ(C₁ ⊕ C₂) ≥ Φ(C₁) + Φ(C₂)` and showed equality fails in
general.

> **Conjecture C5.** Equality `Φ(C₁ ⊕ C₂) = Φ(C₁) + Φ(C₂)` holds **iff** `C₁`
> and `C₂` admit a common minimizing bipartition.

Test: the `←` direction is immediate from `crossInfo_add`; the `→` direction
needs that the superposed minimizer simultaneously minimizes both summands.
Falsifiable by exhibiting a common-minimizer pair with strict inequality.

## Research Brief: Submodularity of Directed Cut Functionals via Edge Decomposition

### Problem Statement
Prove that the directed cut functional on a finite directed graph with non-negative edge weights is submodular, and that restricted minimum lifts preserve submodularity.

### Mathematical Context
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed graph with weight function w : E → ℝ≥0. Define the **directed cut functional**:

crossInfo(S) = Σ_{(u,v) ∈ E, u ∈ S, v ∉ S} w(u,v)

This counts the total weight of edges leaving S.

A set function f : Set α → ℝ is **submodular** if for all S, T:
f(S ∩ T) + f(S ∪ T) ≤ f(S) + f(T)

### Main Results to Prove

**Theorem 1 (crossInfo_submodular):** For any finite directed graph with non-negative edge weights, crossInfo is submodular.

Proof strategy (NO circular reasoning):
1. For a single edge e = (u,v), define the indicator I_e(S) = 1 if u ∈ S and v ∉ S, else 0.
2. Prove the **Edge Indicator Lemma**: For any edge e and any sets S, T ⊆ V, I_e(S ∩ T) + I_e(S ∪ T) ≤ I_e(S) + I_e(T). # Causal Integration Algebra — Submodularity of the Cut Functional

This file extends `Shared.CausalIntegration.Core` with the structural backbone of
the IIT ↔ holographic-entanglement dictionary: the directed cut functional
`crossInfo` is **submodular**, and the abstract "upward min-lift" of any
submodular set function is again submodular (the engine behind discrete
Ryu–Takayanagi strong subadditivity).

Main results:
- `crossInfo_submodular` : the cut-and-paste inequality
  `crossInfo (S ∩ T) + crossInfo (S ∪ T) ≤ crossInfo S + crossInfo T`.
- `minLift_submodular`   : if `f` is submodular then `A ↦ min_{S ⊇ A} f S` is

-- !-- Lab Notes — Cycle target category: CROSS-DOMAIN BRIDGE -- !--
-- !-- Bridges  IIT integrated information (Catalog/Shared/CausalIntegration)

--    set function on bipartitions, is submodular; and minimum-cuts inherit

--    pointwise indicator inequality weighted by the nonneg edge weights. -- !--

-- !-- ANALYSIS (Stage 3).  Submodularity is TRUE and clean.  The *literal* C1
--    holographic min-lift over {S : A ⊆ S} is degenerate for crossInfo because
--    `crossInfo univ = 0`, so the unrestricted lift is identically 0.  The
--    non-trivial version must exclude `S = univ`, but that family is not closed
--    under union — the real obstruction.  We therefore isolate the abstract,
--    true engine `minLift_submodular` (over the full family) and record the
--    restriction problem as a future direction. -- !--

-- !-- CRITIQUE (Stage 4).  `crossInfo_submodular` is non-trivial: its proof needs
--    a genuine pointwise case analysis on the four membership flags, not `simp`.
--    `minLift_submodular` uses attainment of a finite minimum and lattice
--    closure, not definitional unfolding.  Neither is vacuous. -- !--

--    to the full submodular structure required by every holographic conjecture
--    (C1–C5). -- !--
